We can allocate one senior hardware engineer and one firmware engineer part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our lab equipment and internal board archives under NDA.

citations.quote: Jelena Marković
Packaging material permeability screening for MAP of mixed-berry trays

Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios.

Her research integrates food engineering, packaging science, and predictive microbiology to extend the shelf life of perishable horticultural products, with a particular focus on Serbian soft fruits. She has extensive experience developing modified atmosphere packaging systems and mathematical models for microbial growth kinetics in cold-chain logistics. Professor Marković has collaborated with multiple Serbian fruit exporters on industrial packaging trials

proposal.rationale: FreshPak Solutions' raspberry shipments to Germany develop Botrytis mould by day 9 instead of reaching the target of day 14. The company suspects micro-condensation combined with oxygen-transmission rate (OTR) mismatched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C. FreshPak possesses OTR/CO₂TR measurement instruments and two seasons of shipment temperature, humidity, and inspection data, but lacks modelling expertise to translate gas measurements into film specifications. Jelena Marković's published work directly addresses this gap: she systematically screened 12 polymeric films by OTR and CO₂TR, measured headspace equilibrium over eight days, and demonstrated that a film with OTR 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day reduced mould incidence by 55% relative to control. She used finite element modelling to confirm gas permeation trends and predict equilibrium under alternative scenarios—precisely FreshPak's knowledge gap. The technical mechanism is that OTR and CO₂TR values matched to berry respiration rate establish a headspace atmosphere suppressing Botrytis growth and reducing internal condensation. Transfer remains a hypothesis because film performance depends on punnet geometry (125 g rPET), fill mass, seal integrity, and actual cold-chain thermal profiles—variables not yet tested in FreshPak's shipment conditions. Marković's bio confirms extensive collaboration with Serbian fruit exporters and openness to joint projects and industrial PhD supervision.

proposal.rationale: FreshPak Solutions' raspberry shipments to Germany develop Botrytis mould by day 9 instead of reaching day 14. The company suspects micro-condensation combined with oxygen-transmission rate (OTR) mismatched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C. FreshPak possesses OTR/CO₂TR instruments and two seasons of shipment data but lacks modelling expertise. Jelena Marković's published work directly addresses this gap: she screened 12 polymeric films by OTR and CO₂TR, measured headspace equilibrium over eight days, and demonstrated that a film with OTR 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day reduced mould incidence by 55% relative to control. She used finite element modelling to confirm gas permeation and predict equilibrium—precisely FreshPak's need. The technical mechanism is that OTR and CO₂TR values matched to berry respiration establish headspace atmosphere suppressing Botrytis and reducing condensation risk. Transfer remains a hypothesis because film performance depends on punnet geometry (125 g rPET), fill mass, seal integrity, and actual cold-chain thermal profiles—variables not yet tested in FreshPak's conditions. Marković's bio confirms extensive Serbian fruit-exporter collaboration and openness to joint projects.

plan.question: Can finite element modelling-optimized film specifications (OTR 2,000–4,500 cm³/m²/day, CO₂TR 15,000–20,000 cm³/m²/day) reduce Botrytis mould incidence below 1% at day 14 in FreshPak's 125 g rPET punnet under simulated 0–14 °C cold-chain conditions? If yes, does evidence support a conditional industrial PhD investigating microbial-growth prediction with variable seal integrity and thermal profiles?
plan.experiment: Three candidate films (OTR/CO₂TR documented) tested in 14-day controlled chamber trials (±1 °C, ±3% RH) vs. baseline film. Respiration rate measured at 2–4 °C per established protocol. Headspace O₂/CO₂ sampled every 2–3 days; finite element model validated against measured composition (target RMSE <0.5 kPa O₂). Botrytis CFU and visual incidence scored at harvest (day 14). Model then fitted to FreshPak's two-season historical temperature/humidity logs to predict actual destination mould rates. Go/no-go gate at Week 8: if ≥1 trial achieves ≤1% mould at day 14 AND model accuracy ≥80%, proceed to historical validation; otherwise document findings and assess pilot viability.
